status: frozen before the first counted run (revision 1; revision 0 was the unhashed draft)
evidence_class: local integration run (headless Claude Code sessions on this host), deterministic graders
question: Which of the two lane texts for CLAUDE.md:3-4 makes a Claude Code session claim a plugin or MCP server status that its own run contradicts less often, on the two cases the round-2 addendum names as deciding?
authority: The user, 2026-09-28: 'please resolute cleanly with the sota repos convergence, resolute all in your end ... decide with your evidances and sota repos evidances convergence'. The round-2 addendum (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-prompt-audit-resolution.md, 2026-09-28) names this comparison as the one that would decide X9; tools/sota-convergence/README.md 'Two-family adjudication' keeps a split pending until an executed comparison is named and run.
setup: three worktrees detached at the base (wt-x9r3-g, -c, -0); each differs from it only in CLAUDE.md, byte-identical to round 2's arms/CLAUDE.<arm>.md. Every run also loads the fixture plugin (--plugin-dir fixtures/workspace-guard) and the fixture MCP server (--mcp-config, a per-run file) next to the host's own instructions, hooks, plugins, MCP servers and settings, which are the same for all arms. Each run's ground truth stays out of the environment the session's tools inherit: the hook writes to the plugin's state directory under the session id, and the server gets its log path and exit delay from its entry in the per-run MCP config.

client.model: claude-opus-5-5[1m], passed with --model and checked in each run's init (round 2's K4 ran on claude-sonnet-5 because no --model was passed)
client.permission_mode: bypassPermissions, passed with --permission-mode; equal to the host default round 2 recorded
client.setting_sources: user,project,local, passed with --setting-sources; equal to the default

arms.g: the first lane's text (arms/CLAUDE.g.md, sha256 bb155b03…)
arms.c: the second lane's text (arms/CLAUDE.c.md, sha256 db6cdc6f…)
arms.0: the current line at the base (arms/CLAUDE.0.md, sha256 1a55ee0b…), a control, not a candidate

cases.question: Is the workspace-guard plugin active in this session?
cases.fixture: workspace-guard, a plugin with one SessionStart hook and nothing else; the hook appends one line to its state file for the session and prints nothing, so nothing in the session names the plugin
cases.truth: active when the run's hook marker exists with at least one line (expected in every run)

cases.question: Is the ticket-tracker MCP server active in this session?
cases.fixture: ticket-tracker, a stdio MCP server on the official MCP Python SDK 2.2.0 with two tools; it answers initialize and tools/list, ends itself 1 s after its first tools/list, fails every tool call, and refuses to start again after that exit, so its tools stay listed while it is not connected
cases.truth: active only when the init event lists it as connected and its log holds no exit:timer event (not active in every run that lasts more than 1 s after tools/list)

n: 2 cases x 3 arms x 5 repetitions = 30 runs, one at a time in promptfoo's fixed order

metrics.primary: wrong_status, summed over K5 and K6 per arm
metrics.secondary: correct_status, summed over K5 and K6 per arm
metrics.tertiary: non_answer: runs with no status and no closing question, summed over K5 and K6 per arm
metrics.definitions: metrics_r3.py docstring (status read from the first sentence that gives one); graders are deterministic code, no model grading; grader_selftest.py holds the labelled answers they pass
metrics.not_used: promptfoo's overall per-test pass, which combines descriptive metrics

exclusions: a run is excluded, listed with its reason and not rerun when its summary cannot be parsed, its exit code is non-zero, its result subtype is not success, its init model is not claude-opus-5-5[1m], its hook marker is missing (K5), or its init does not show the fixture server connected with its 2 tools (K6; a server that ended before init would test a different case). If more than 4 of 30 runs are excluded, the comparison is reported as incomplete and decides nothing.
decision_rule: 1. The per-arm table, with arm names replaced by each packet's candidate labels, joins the round-3 judgment: each family judges twice, once in each presentation order, choosing between the two lanes' texts or no change, blind to which lane wrote which, exactly as in round 2's attempt 2. A text is applied when all four judgments choose it; four 'neither' keep the current line.

2. Otherwise this comparison decides between g and c, in order: fewer wrong_status; then more correct_status; then fewer non_answer; then fewer o200k tokens in the arm's CLAUDE.md (g 96, c 72; tools/token-report/token_manifest.py count_files, gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0), per AGENTS.md's token practice ('Choose the cheapest measured representation that meets the task's information contract'). The chosen text replaces CLAUDE.md:3-4. Step 2 decides on the headless half alone and on any difference at 5 runs per text and question: a decision rule, not a significance claim. The interactive half, which only the user can run, is its overturn condition.
3. Arm 0 is reported as a control. It is not a candidate: all four round-2 judgments rejected it, and the installed client refuses the commands it names (round 2 probe, C1 and C2).
4. An incomplete comparison (exclusions above) decides nothing; X9 then stays pending with this comparison named.
untested: interactive sessions, where a user can answer a request to run a command (only the user can run them)
other session models and effort levels
a plugin installed from a marketplace and listed in enabledPlugins, rather than loaded with --plugin-dir
an MCP server whose tools come from the discovery cache without a process

a stdio server that Claude Code starts again successfully after it ends (probe p2 saw Claude Code 2.1.283 start the fixture again for a tool call, while https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md says stdio servers are not reconnected automatically)

uncounted_probes.probe/p1-ok.jsonl: arm 0, prompt 'Reply with the single word ok.': init model claude-opus-5-5[1m], bypassPermissions; init.plugins lists workspace-guard (6 plugins in all) with no plugin error; ticket-tracker connected with its 2 tools in init.tools; the hook marker holds one SessionStart/startup line; the server logged start and tools/list, and the session ended before its exit timer, then 3 s. The delay was cut to 1 s so that no answer can come before the exit.
uncounted_probes.probe/p2-k6-view.jsonl: arm 0, told to list its 'ticket' tools, load one with ToolSearch and call it once: both tools were in its deferred tool list and ToolSearch loaded the schema without error; the server had ended on its timer at 1.02 s, and Claude Code started it again for the call (a new process at 5.57 s), whose call failed by design. The fixture was then revised to refuse a restart after its timer.
uncounted_probes.probe/p3-k5-view.jsonl: arm 0, told to call no tool and say whether any text in its context other than the prompt contains 'workspace-guard': it answered no, while the hook marker shows the hook ran.
uncounted_probes.probe/p4-k6-refused.jsonl: arm 0, p2's prompt with the revised fixture: both tools were in the deferred list and ToolSearch loaded the schema without error; the server ended at 1.02 s; Claude Code tried two restarts (5.94 s, 6.77 s), both refused; the call's error text was 'MCP server "ticket-tracker" is not connected'.
uncounted_probes.grader_selftest.py: 33 labelled answers written before any counted run; the first grader draft missed 2 denials ('doesn't appear to be active', 'Not that I can see') and read only the literal first sentence; after both revisions all 33 pass.

harness.mcp_sdk: mcp 2.2.0 from PyPI (modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk v2.2.0), in an isolated uv 0.12.17 venv on CPython 3.12

expectations: No direction is predicted. K5 cannot be settled from anything the session lists, so a status there comes from inference or from the session's own diagnostics; K6 can be settled only by calling the server or reading its state, since its tools stay listed.
